markscheme.html:
B

A simple pendulum released from rest is at its maximum displacement. It reaches maximum speed when it passes through the equilibrium position, which occurs after one-quarter of a period (T/4). The period of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2π√(L/g). Using L = 10 m and approximating g ≈ 10 m/s² (a common simplification in multiple-choice questions to yield clean answers), the period is T = 2π√(10/10) = 2π s. The time to reach maximum speed is therefore t = T/4 = 2π/4 = π/2 s.

question.html: A simple pendulum of length 10 m is released from rest at time t = 0, at a small angle from the vertical. At what value of t, in seconds, will the pendulum reach its maximum speed?
